characteristics.roast: Medium to heavy, often multi-stage roasting

description.short: Old-bush Shui Xian celebrated for its signature mossy (taixian) and deeply resonant woody complexity
description.overview: Bush age is the defining dimension of this tea: the extensive root systems of gnarly, moss-draped bushes undisturbed for decades yield remarkable depth and an inimitable mossy woodland character unavailable in younger plants.
description.leaf: Large, dark-brown, rugged twisted leaves, often thicker and more irregular than standard Shui Xian
description.liquor: Deep amber to rich mahogany, thick and viscous infusion
description.aroma: Moss, damp bark, aged timber, forest floor, and warm subtle spice
description.taste: Dense, viscous, layered with iconic moss (tai xian) notes, profound stony minerality, and completely free of rough astringency
description.aftertaste: Extremely lingering and warming, filled with soothing throat richness and sweet minerality
description.processing: Follows traditional rock tea craftsmanship, exclusively sourcing leaves from ancient, untamed bushes left to grow naturally without heavy pruning

history.origin: The designation 'Lao Cong' ('Old Bush') was popularized by local growers to distinguish tea plucked from ancient, semi-wild Shui Xian groves from standard cultivated plantation bushes.
history.development: For decades, these low-yielding old bushes were neglected in favor of faster-growing plantings, until the 2000s when connoisseurs and collectors rediscovered their unique mossy terroir signature.
history.modern: Today, Lao Cong Shui Xian is among the most sought-after collector teas in Wuyi, frequently labeled with specific historical micro-plots and grove names.
interestingFacts: To qualify as authentic 'Lao Cong', bushes generally must be at least 60 years old, with premier grade lots harvested from centenary trees over 100 years of age.
The term 'Taixian Xiang' (苔藓香, moss fragrance) has become the gold-standard sensory descriptor exclusively reserved for high-grade old-bush Shui Xian.
